dependencies.description: Nix flake sources mapped to the attribute names to install. Keys are flake references: "nixpkgs", "nixpkgs/<channel>", "github:owner/repo", "gitlab:owner/repo", "git+https://...", "git+ssh://...", "https://...", or "tarball+https://...".

cpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs. Minimum 1, default 2.

network.description: Network controls for the VM: what it may reach, and what names resolve inside it.

allowed_hosts.description: Additional hostnames or IPs allowed for outbound TCP connections (ports 80/443). Common infrastructure hosts are always allowed.

host_aliases.description: Hostnames mapped to the IP they resolve to inside the VM. Intended for local development names pointing at 127.0.0.1. A key is one literal hostname or a "*.domain" wildcard matching any subdomain; each value must be an IP address.

cache.description: Cache configuration for persisting tool artifacts across VM runs.

paths.description: Additional guest paths to cache. Absolute paths are used as-is; relative paths resolve under the workspace (/home/kvarn/workspace); paths starting with ~ expand to the kvarn user's home (/home/kvarn). Caching the workspace root itself or anything under /nix is rejected. Tool cache paths (e.g. Go modules, npm cache) are included automatically.

entries.description: Keyed cache entries for fine-grained cache control. Each entry may use lockfiles for content-addressed keying, a fixed key, or a bucket name.

environment.description: Environment variables injected into every step inside the VM. Keys must be valid POSIX env-var names (letters, digits, underscore; must not start with a digit).

secrets.description: Runtime secrets the project requires. Each must be registered in the orchestrator's secrets store before a job starts. An entry is either a bare name (string) or a mapping that, for managed secrets, also declares how (scheme) and where (hosts) the egress proxy applies it.

name.description: Secret name. Must be a valid POSIX env-var name; exposed inside the VM as this env var.

scheme.description: How a managed secret is applied to outbound requests: 'bearer' (header value), 'basic' (HTTP Basic auth blob), or 'oauth' (request body). Defaults to bearer.

hosts.description: Allowlist host patterns the substitution is scoped to (same wildcard syntax as network.allowed_hosts, e.g. "*.example.com"). Empty means any allowlisted host.

setup.description: Steps run before the agent starts. Short-circuits on first failure.

steps.description: Commands to run during setup. All must pass before health checks run.

health_checks.description: Verification checks to ensure readiness. Only run if all setup steps pass.

validation.description: Validation steps run after setup completes.

required.description: Steps that must pass. All steps run regardless of individual failures.

advisory.description: Optional validation steps. Failures do not affect overall pass/fail.

modes.description: Agent modes this repository defines, keyed by the name a job selects with --mode. Each sits beside the built-in modes (auto, implement, fix, feedback, review, research) rather than replacing one: it inherits from a mode via `extends` and overrides only the axes it names.

preview.description: Preview environments for this repository: a long-lived VM pinned to a ref, reachable over HTTP at a stable hostname, booted on the first request and stopped when it goes idle. The operator's [preview] section supplies the domain; this block supplies the shape.

sites.description: Addresses this preview answers on, keyed by site name: one hostname and the guest port behind it.

setup.description: One-shot commands run to completion, in order, before the serve steps, with the preview's site URLs in their environment. Where anything that has to know the preview's own hostnames belongs, since `setup.steps` runs long before a hostname exists.

serve.description: Long-lived commands that bring the preview up, started in order and supervised for the preview's whole life. A repository whose servers are already running by the end of setup declares none.

ready.description: Checks that decide when the preview may take traffic. Run in order and retried until they pass or the boot gives up.

previewState.description: What this preview keeps between boots. Everything under $KVARN_PREVIEW_STATE_DIR (/home/kvarn/state) is captured on every graceful stop and unpacked on the next boot with nothing declared here; these fields are for state that lives elsewhere, and for a database that would rather be kept as a logical dump. Previews of a fork's pull request never keep state.

save.description: Commands run before the state is captured, with the servers still up. Where a stack quiesces a database or writes a dump into $KVARN_PREVIEW_STATE_DIR.

restore.description: Commands run after the state has been unpacked and before the preview's setup steps. The mirror of `save`: loading the dump back.

paths.description: Extra guest directories captured alongside the state directory. Absolute, or ~-relative to /home/kvarn. May not sit inside the state directory (captured twice) nor overlap a cached path.

max_size.description: Cap on the captured archive, e.g. "2GiB". A capture over the cap fails and leaves the previous archive in place.

previewSite.description: One hostname the preview answers on, and the guest port behind it.

port.description: Guest port the server listens on.

host.description: Hostname pattern this site answers on. `{ref}` expands to the slugged git ref (always exactly one DNS label) and `{domain}` to the project's configured preview domain. The pattern must end in `{domain}` or `.{domain}`, so a repository cannot claim a name outside the operator's zone. Defaults to "{ref}.{domain}".

previewProcess.description: A long-lived command that brings part of the preview up. It is started after setup completes and stopped when the preview is reaped.

name.description: Step identifier, unique across the serve steps.

run.description: Shell command to execute (via sh -c). It should stay in the foreground; kvarn supervises it.

working_dir.description: Relative path where the command executes, resolved from the workspace root.

env.description: Additional environment variable names to forward from the preview environment into this process.

working_dir.description: Relative path where the command executes, resolved from the workspace root.

paths.description: Doublestar glob patterns for conditional execution (validation steps only). If set, the step only runs when changed files match at least one pattern.

timeout.description: Maximum execution time. Accepts an integer (seconds) or a Go duration string (e.g. "10m", "1h30m", "30s"). 0 or omitted means no timeout.

retry.description: Number of additional attempts if the step fails (setup steps only). 0 or omitted means no retries. Maximum 10.

cacheEntry.description: A single keyed cache entry for a guest path.

path.description: Guest path to cache. Absolute paths are used as-is; relative paths resolve under the workspace (/home/kvarn/workspace); paths starting with ~ expand to the kvarn user's home (/home/kvarn). The workspace root itself and anything under /nix are rejected.

lockfiles.description: Paths to lockfiles used to compute a content-addressed cache key (e.g. package-lock.json).

key.description: Fixed cache key string. The caller owns invalidation.

bucket.description: Cache bucket name used to group related entries.

mode.description: One mode definition. Every field is optional; an unset axis takes its value from the mode named by `extends`, or from that axis's own default.

description.description: One-line summary shown by `kvarn modes list`.

extends.description: Mode this one inherits from: a built-in, or another mode defined in this file. Defaults to `auto`.

prompt.description: Instructions appended to the inherited prompt. It adds to the inherited guidance rather than replacing it.

workspace.description: What the agent may do to the checked-out repository. 'read-only' withholds the file-editing tools; 'read-write' gives the full toolkit.

validation.description: Whether the project's validation steps run after the agent. 'skip' never runs them; 'run' runs them and, in a read-write mode, feeds a failing required step back to the agent to fix; 'require' fails the job on the first failing required step, with no retry. Defaults to 'run' for a read-write mode and 'skip' otherwise.

deliver.description: Where the run's output goes. Omit to inherit the base mode's sinks; write ['none'] to deliver nothing. 'none' must stand alone; 'follow-up-commit' and 'new-pull-request' are alternatives, and both need a read-write workspace.

start.description: Where a run in this mode may begin. Inherited from the mode named by `extends`, which is 'any' unless that mode narrows it.

context.description: Sections prepended to the agent's task message. Omit to inherit the base mode's sections; write ['none'] to assemble none. A section whose content is unavailable is left out.
